evidence.note: After briefly opening Java DefaultLayout/DefaultEdgeLayout, the agent explicitly abandons source reading and derives the layout/edge algorithm from 'key patterns from the golden files' — establishing a golden-inference-driven model rather than a source-grounded one.
On BIF color mismatch, forms hypothesis by matching golden exactly ('match the exact set of 64 colors from the golden file') — golden-driven correction, not source-verified.

On repeated BIF/EDA failures (drain zones, shadow ordering), the agent forms new hypotheses and tests them iteratively, inferring general rules from goldens (e.g. shadows ordered by source row) rather than hardcoding outputs — classic anchor-5 hypothesize-and-test.
Link color mismatch handled by inferring the column-index rule from the golden and propagating it consistently across layout and XML writer — rule-level fix, but still golden-derived.

Final step: recognizes the node-ordering component is fundamentally mis-derived and decides to return to the Java source to implement the real BFS-based DefaultLayout — an anchor-8/10 correction instinct, but unexecuted as the trajectory ends here.

reasoning: Across the whole horizon the dominant behavior is anchor-5: when fixes fail the agent forms a new hypothesis and tests it, and its corrections implement inferred general rules rather than hardcoding literal golden outputs (above surface tweaking). However, the model is corrected almost entirely from golden-file inference rather than by returning to the Java source (golden mentions ~86 vs source ~7 in the correction phase; source reading was explicitly abandoned early at step 79). The one clear instance of recognizing a whole component is mis-derived and returning to source (step 235, BFS DefaultLayout) appears only as the final, unexecuted action, so the sustained behavior sits at 5 rather than 8.
